mechanism_narrative: Sustained grocery and pharmacy mobility above baseline (+1.6 to +14.3 percent) indicates consistent essential-goods purchasing behavior that anchors foot traffic to retail corridors, driving retail-and-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks as consumers combine trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM positive in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below baseline in more than two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has recovered to positive territory (+6.3 percent at t-0w) after sustained negative values, signaling consumer confidence in outdoor activity resumption. This confidence spillover increases willingness to visit retail-and-recreation venues within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive and remains positive
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +6.3 at t-0w after -13.3 at t-3w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility returns to negative values within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the baseline period.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has collapsed sharply to -38.3 percent at t-1w, indicating widespread remote work or closure. This suppresses commute-based retail incidence and reduces weekday foot traffic, driving retail-and-recreation mobility downward over the next four weeks as the work-from-home regime persists.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers to above -20 percent within two weeks and RETAIL_REC increases relative to the baseline period.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility remains persistently depressed (-18.1 percent at t-1w, -9.6 at t-0w), indicating reduced public transportation use. When transit is suppressed, retail-and-recreation venues dependent on transit access experience lower foot traffic, producing negative RETAIL_REC momentum over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -8 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT negative in all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above -5 percent and remains there for two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases relative to the baseline period.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility elevation (+3.4 to +6.1 percent) combined with workplace collapse (-38.3 percent at t-1w) indicates a shift to home-based activity. This dual signal suppresses retail-and-recreation visits as consumers remain sheltered, producing downward pressure on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > +3 percent AND WORKPLACES < -30 percent simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated while WORKPLACES collapsed at t-1w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers above -20 percent within two weeks, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +2 percent, or RETAIL_REC increases relative to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility surge to +14.3 percent at t-0w (holiday season purchasing) combined with parks recovery (+6.3 percent) signals seasonal consumer engagement. This dual positive signal drives retail-and-recreation mobility upward over the next two weeks as holiday shopping and outdoor leisure peak.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > +10 percent AND PARKS > +5 percent in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:Both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS positive at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5 percent within one week, or PARKS returns to negative, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to baseline over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Transit suppression (-9.6 percent at t-0w) persists despite modest workplace recovery from -38.3 to -12.7 percent, indicating policy-driven transit restrictions or consumer avoidance independent of work reopening. This decoupling maintains retail-and-recreation suppression over the next two weeks as transit-dependent retail access remains constrained.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -8 percent while WORKPLACES improves by >20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered 25.6 points from t-1w to t-0w while TRANSIT remained depressed
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above -5 percent within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases relative to baseline despite transit suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation mobility has stabilized at -12.9 percent (t-0w) after declining from -17.4 percent (t-3w), indicating a floor effect. This stabilization at a depressed level, absent strong positive signals from WORKPLACES or TRANSIT recovery, suggests retail-and-recreation will remain suppressed over the next week as the floor persists.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC variance across last two weeks < 1 percent AND RETAIL_REC < -10 percent
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -12.9 in both t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in the next week, or WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover by >10 points simultaneously.
